basis: Independent observation of the actual original PNG, once, at original resolution, before constructing modern geometry.
coordinateConvention: Approximate observed source pixels; origin at top left; y increases downwards. These are descriptive observations, not printed measured givens.

observedStructure.fact: One inverted-U bent conductor, not two unrelated vertical bars. Heavy outer boundary rises from roughly (70,425), rounds over (185,17), and returns to (300,428). Heavy inner boundary rises from roughly (127,425), rounds over (185,75), and returns to (241,428). Two bottom transverse caps join the respective boundaries. The top bend and both long straight arms belong to the same conductor.

Three complete nested, thinner inverted-U field lines between the heavy boundaries. Approximate paired arm x positions are (84,286), (99,271), (113,256); bend apexes are near y32, y47, y61. All three rise along the left arm, turn continuously around the top, and descend along the right arm. Each has one upward arrow on the left and one downward arrow on the right. They do not terminate at the bend, jump between tracks, or cross the conductor boundary.

Four right-directed upward-arching exterior field curves cross the white opening between the inner arms. The top one has the strongest arch, with ends near (128,177) and (241,178), apex near (184,142). The next ends near y232/y235 and apex y213. The third ends near y317/y319 and apex y300. The bottom ends near y404/y409 and apex y390. Each has exactly one arrow near the middle pointing right. These are outside the conductor, not transverse internal field vectors. They meet the inner surfaces obliquely.

Three distinct exterior curved branches meet the left outer boundary, approximately near y155, y240 and y387. Each bends out toward the upper left and has one arrow near its far exterior end. All three arrowheads point upper-left, away from the boundary. Approximate far ends are (28,28), (17,156), (15,313).

Three distinct exterior curved branches meet the right outer boundary, approximately near y154, y253 and y380. Their far exterior ends are near (354,28), (351,164), (350,319). All three arrowheads point lower-left, toward the right boundary. Do not mirror the left arrows into outward right arrows.

modernRegularization: Replace rough scan strokes with deterministic continuous JSXGraph circular arcs and segments; source curve topology, nesting, arm-to-gap proportions, arch ordering, joins and arrow directions remain facts.
Regularize left/right arm bottom alignment, bend center and smoothly tangent arc joins without asserting printed radii, exact symmetry, numerical dimensions or electric-field magnitudes.
Use semantic ink for conductor boundaries and accent for field curves; no legends, charge signs, current labels, extra givens, apparatus or new visible prose.
teachingPurpose: With the complete frozen lesson, preserve tangential internal steady-current fields around a bend and oblique exterior fields on both the inner and outer surfaces. The white opening is exterior space, not conductor material.
uncertainty: Pixel coordinates and arrowhead tip extents are approximate because the scan is coarse. Direction, count, nesting, boundary topology and the location inside versus outside conductor material are clear. No measured value is inferred.
